title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes.

HPI
The patient is a 78-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of his type 2 diabetes mellitus. He reports that his blood glucose levels have been consistently high over the past month. He notes that he has been diligent with his current regimen but feels his glucose remains out of control despite his efforts. He denies any acute symptoms of illness or recent changes in his health status.

Medication List
Long-acting insulin.

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. He is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. Skin is intact without lesions. Vital signs are stable.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: The patient is experiencing hyperglycemia. His current management with insulin alone has not been sufficient to maintain target glucose levels.

Plan
1. Continue current insulin regimen.
2. Increase insulin dose as tolerated to address hyperglycemia.
3. Patient will monitor fingerstick glucose levels twice daily and keep a log for review at the next visit.
4. Follow up in four weeks.

Electronically signed, R. Mensah, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Diabetes documented as poorly controlled, out of control, or with hyperglycemia is coded to diabetes with hyperglycemia.
Long-term insulin use in type 2 diabetes: add Z79.4.

distractors.why: Hyperglycemia is a complication with its own code.
Z79.4 is required for routine insulin use in type 2 diabetes.
